text:
Maya: quick q — yesterday we had a rollout configured in the console (10% canary -> 90% stable) but an app-level feature flag seems to have flipped and all traffic hit the canary. who should win when both exist?
Samir: console rollout should be authoritative for traffic routing. flags are feature toggles, not traffic managers. that said, there are merge-order subtleties. :thinking:
Maya: yeah that's our expectation, but logs show user-assignment came from the flag evaluation at request time.
Liam: do we know the evaluation order? runtime may re-eval flags on KV refresh and overwrite previously-decided routing key.
Samir: current RoutingService merge logic: we apply base route -> app config flags -> console rollouts, last writer wins. i think that's reversed for safety.
Samir: quick snippet of the problematic logic:
```
mergeOrder = ['default', 'app_flag', 'console_rollout']
result = mergeLayers(mergeOrder)
```
Maya: so console_rollout should be checked first and be final, not the other way.
Anya: product standpoint: console rollouts are the controlled release instrument. app flags are for dev/experiments and shouldn't override production rollout splits.
Daria: UI/UX note — we should surface source precedence in the rollout panel. a small badge "source: console (authoritative)" and a warning when you create a rollout that conflicts with existing flags.
Samir: agree. propose we change merge order to: `['console_rollout', 'app_flag', 'default']` and add a hard guard that prevents flags from increasing traffic beyond console guard thresholds.
Liam: i'll take the runtime changes to ensure evaluation honors the new precedence and that KV refresh doesn't stomp assignments mid-request. i'll add an integration test that simulates a KV update during traffic assignment.
Maya: who owns the server-side merge change? @Samir?
Samir: i'll open the PR in eng-platform/routing-service. will include unit tests for the three-layer merge and a couple of regression cases where KV reload used to flip routes.
Anya: also can we emit telemetry on conflicts? e.g., `rollout.conflict_detected` with tags {route, flag_id, rollout_id, user_bucket} so we can alert if this ever happens in prod.
Samir: yes. plan: add `routing.conflict` event and a `source` field on evaluation output (values: console, app_flag, default). also add a severity metric for conflicts.
Daria: i'll prototype the UI badge + a tooltip that explains precedence and a small modal that pops up on conflict creation saying "This route has an existing flag that may override behaviour — console rollouts take precedence". mock: figma.com/file/abcd1234
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: routing-service staging deploy started v1.3.2-rc.4 :rocket:
Maya: should we also guard quotas so a mis-set flag can't suddenly route >50% to a canary?
Samir: good point. i'll add a policy check during merge: if flag_request > rollout.max_allowed -> clamp to rollout.max_allowed and emit `routing.clamped_by_rollout`.
Liam: i'll coordinate to add an end-to-end test (runtime + routing-service) that asserts clamping behaviour. will link tests in PR.
Samir: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/eng-platform/pull/1234 — implements precedence change, conflict telemetry, clamp logic.
Liam: runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/567 — ensures KV refresh doesn't overwrite authoritative assignment. integration test here: github.com/redwood-inference/tests/commit/9a8b7c
Daria: UI branch: github.com/redwood-inference/console/tree/feature/rollout-source-badge with screenshots in PR.
Maya: thanks all. please ping here when staging has the full stack (routing + runtime + console) so we can run a controlled canary and validate. :thumbsup:
